title: Cross-region burst choreography and latency corridor roadmap
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Objective: Define and deliver a quarterly roadmap for cross-region burst choreography and explicit latency corridors for Dedicated pools so customer applications experience predictable tail latency during global surge events while minimizing excess reserved capacity.

Scope: This initiative covers roadmap planning, experiments, and canary playbook to coordinate: (1) cross-region request routing policies (smart routing + fallbacks), (2) predictive prewarm and reservoir activation choreography, (3) explicit latency 'corridor' SLOs for Dedicated customers with burst patterns, and (4) operational runbooks and console controls to visualize corridor occupancy and cross-region failover.

Success metrics: 
- 99th percentile per-request latency within defined corridor during synthetic 3x burst tests (target: < 250ms increase over steady-state for Tier-1 customers).
- Reduction in average reserved capacity overhead during tested workloads by >= 12% versus current baseline (measured on identical replayed traffic).
- Canary rollouts that detect regression within 15 minutes and automatically revert or shift traffic to fallback region.

Milestones (quarter):
- Week 1-3: Alignment & design doc with infra/eng (routing policies, fallbacks, and metrics).
- Week 4-6: Implement prototype choreography in staging (engine + control-plane hooks).
- Week 7-9: Run synthetic cross-region surge experiments, iterate on prewarm thresholds.
- Week 10-12: Console UX: corridor visualization and per-route corridor tuning.
- Week 13: Canary plan, runbook, and soft launch to pilot customers.

Stakeholders: PM (Priya Natarajan), Eng leads (Serving runtime: Diego Morales, Routing: Aisha Khan), SRE (Marco Li), Console product/design (Janelle Park), Solutions Eng for pilot enablement (Rahul Desai).

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Over-aggressive prewarming increases cost; underprewarm risks higher tail latency. Will mitigate via closed-loop experiments and cost/loss dashboards.
- Cross-region failovers add complexity to KV cache consistency for long-lived chat sessions; plan includes session affinity heuristics and TTL-based cache invalidation during failover.
- Regulatory constraints may limit cross-region routing for some customers; build explicit opt-out flag and VPC guardrails.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Cross-Region+Burst+Choreography+Design
- Experiment dashboard (internal Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated/burst-choreo-experiments
- Prototype PR (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4872
- Pilot customer checklist (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D

Open questions to resolve in week 1:
- What are the latency corridor bands (Tier-1 vs Tier-2)? Proposal: Tier-1 corridor = steady-state p99 + 200ms; Tier-2 = steady-state p99 + 400ms.
- How to represent corridor occupancy in the console without overwhelming SRE curves? Proposed: single normalized occupancy metric + per-route drilldowns.

Next steps (actionable):
- Schedule alignment workshop with Eng & SRE by 2026-03-05 (owner: Priya).
- Create experiment harness for cross-region 3x burst by 2026-03-20 (owner: Diego).
- Draft console mockups for corridor visualization by 2026-03-25 (owner: Janelle).
